title: Among the Princes, Earthly Gods
description: Among the Princes, Earthly Gods in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 86, headed “A general song of praise to God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-mong the prin-ces, earth-ly gods, There's none hath power di-vine; Nor is their na-ture, might-y Lord, Nor are their works like thine.

lines: Nor is their nature, mighty Lord,
Nor are their works like thine.
The nations thou hast made shall bring
For thou alone dost wondrous things,
Lord, I would walk with holy feet;
And my poor scatter'd thoughts unite
Great is thy mercy, and my tongue
How by thy grace my sinking soul
Rose from the deeps of hell.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
